title.narrative: Scaling-up conservation and sustainable management of priority wetlands of the East-Asian Australasian Flyway in the Philippines (PHIL FLYWAY)

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

To protect, restore, and sustainably manage priority wetland habitats in the Philippine segment of the East Asian-Australasian Flyway to ensure the conservation of migratory waterbirds and overall biodiversity while providing ecosystem goods and services for local communities.

We confirm that the project design has considered socio-economic benefits to be delivered by the project, including provision of livelihood opportunities and climate resiliency with the nature-based solutions. Strengthened wetland management and sustainable financing will contribute to sustainable resource management that willould ensure sustain ecological goods and services in the three priority sites. These were clearly described in the Project Description and will be monitored and reported on during project implementation and terminal evaluation review (TER). The core indicators stated that the project benefits about 328,743 people across the three priority sites. Direct beneficiaries will be from the implemented nature-based solutions and measures to strengthen governance.

participating-org.narrative: Department of Environment and Natural Resources /Biodiversity Management Bureau (DENR-BMB)
